A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same registering method and MITRE models. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–L are readable and can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original EC-40 experiments, MITRE pretraining and fine-tuning evaluations, ablations, and representation analyses, including supplementary results in the appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds quantitative attention analysis, sentence-level representation analysis, and inference-time measurements.

M1.justification: Register initialization, source-aligned register length, attention-mask rules, training objective, and MITRE architectures remain unchanged. The new analyses examine the existing method; the encoder-decoder adaptation already appears in Appendix J of v2.

E1.justification: Both versions retain EC-40/Flores evaluation across 41 languages, 24-language MITRE pretraining, and fine-tuning on 5, 25, and 100 directions. The added diagnostics and timing measurements introduce no documented new language, domain, or translation task.

E2.justification: v3 adds reported timing comparisons against M2M-483M/1.2B and three NLLB sizes in Table 7; v2's numerical inference-overhead comparison uses vanilla Dec-only. Comparator membership in the translation-quality and fine-tuning experiments remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols include attention statistics over 100 random instances at four length ratios, sentence-level cosine analysis over 10 instances, and timing 100 sentences with batch size 1 and beam size 5. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, model configurations, and fine-tuning settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 already contains component ablations, register-length sensitivity, t-SNE plots, and attention examples. v3 deepens these mechanism analyses with attention strength, positional-distance and selection-entropy measurements in Table 6, and layerwise sentence-representation similarities in Figure 6.

E5.justification: v3 newly reports ten repetitions for each inference-timing experiment. Existing training and sampling seeds remain unchanged, and the new timing results provide no standard deviations, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing translation, fine-tuning, and appendix benchmark scores are unchanged. New results include attention-selection entropy of 5.25 at ratio 1 versus 5.15 at 0.75, layerwise cosine trends, and generation times of 85.65 seconds for MITRE-913M and 82.15 seconds for NLLB-3.3B. v2's 1.1-times vanilla-decoder inference-overhead figure is removed; the new timings do not establish a same-setting performance change.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and Equations (1)–(4) remain unchanged. The added empirical diagnostics introduce no new formal assumptions, theoretical results, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: registering addresses off-target translation, MITRE supports 24 languages, competes with commercial LLMs, and adapts effectively through fine-tuning. Additional diagnostic evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 interprets augmentation as diffuse attention, compression as potentially neglecting context, and the new cosine profiles as movement toward target-language representations. Its limitations also replace v2's asserted inference-speed advantage over NLLB with a claim of comparable cost, supported by Table 7.

D1.justification: v3 identifies Hugging Face implementations for the timing comparison and explains mean-pooling token representations and aggregating source-token attention selections. Existing training, hardware, LoRA, prompting, and code/data-access details in the appendices remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive positioning remain the same. Changes such as Fan et al. 2020 to 2021 and Zhu et al. 2023 to 2024 update publication metadata for existing references, rather than introduce new research relationships.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized language edits, updates author affiliation/contact information, and changes the numbered limitation and ethics headings to unnumbered plural headings. The section sequence and appendix organization remain intact, with localized explanatory additions in Section 6.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–7 and Figure 6, relocates several existing displays, and renumbers subsequent appendix material. It clarifies Figure 3's ratio caption and corrects Table 4's appendix reference from B to E; existing benchmark-table designs and plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: Table 6 and Figure 6 add quantitative support for the proposed mechanism. Table 7 makes inference costs inspectable and accompanies a more defensible comparison with NLLB in the limitations. These improve evidential support and precision modestly; small diagnostic samples and absent timing variability limit the gains.
